text: It's a float valve connecting troughs to a pressurised water line. Usually there's a float, a plastic ball or block. It floats on the water and is connected to the lever arm. So when the cows drink, the water level drops, the float sinks, the lever arm tips and it pulls the plunger, washer, whatever, away from the seat. So it opens and the water flows into the trough. As it fills, the float lifts. So it pushes the plunger back, closes the seat, and the opening gets smaller and smaller. And then it closes. When it starts to overflow, it's usually a worn or dirty washer. Or the float is punctured or waterlogged, so it's not lifting enough to close the valve. So it just keeps flowing and overflows.
